# Raspberry Kitchen Radio — Raspberry Pi 3A+ firmware config.
# Installed to the FAT boot partition as config.txt by the Buildroot
# post-image / genimage step.

# Keep the stock Raspberry Pi 3 firmware files explicit while recovering the
# bootable checkpoint. These match Buildroot's upstream raspberrypi3/config_3.txt.
start_file=start.elf
fixup_file=fixup.dat

# Name the kernel image on the FAT boot partition. Our board/radio/post-image.sh
# reads this `kernel=` line (like Buildroot's stock RPi post-image) to know which
# file to place on boot.vfat; without it the generated genimage file list gets an
# empty entry that makes mcopy try to copy the whole images dir into the vfat
# ("Disk full"). 32-bit build ships a zImage (not the 64-bit Image).
kernel=zImage

# Keep the HDMI/framebuffer path debuggable until boot + SSH are proven.
disable_overscan=1
gpu_mem_512=100

# Enable the on-chip Bluetooth radio (Bluetooth A2DP audio source). On the Pi
# 3A+ the CYW43438/BCM4345C0 Bluetooth is attached over a PL011 UART (ttyAMA0).
#
# IMPORTANT — do NOT use `dtoverlay=pi3-miniuart-bt` here. That overlay moves
# Bluetooth onto the *mini-UART* (ttyS0), whose clock/flow-control cannot
# reliably sustain the A2DP data rate: streaming produced continuous
# "Bluetooth: hci0: ACL packet for unknown connection handle" /
# "Unexpected continuation frame (len 0)" kernel errors, ~50% of the audio was
# lost, and playback was choppy then silent. Leaving the overlay OFF keeps
# Bluetooth on the full PL011 (with hardware flow control), which streams A2DP
# cleanly. The kernel console stays on tty1 (see cmdline.txt), so nothing else
# needs the PL011. The BlueZ stack + UART attach come up via /etc/init.d/S42bluetooth.
# dtoverlay=pi3-miniuart-bt   # deliberately NOT set — see note above

# Bring up the PL011 UART deterministically for the Bluetooth attach. (Pinning
# the VPU core clock via core_freq was tried and made no difference on the PL011,
# so it is intentionally NOT set.)
enable_uart=1

# Hardware interfaces the radio needs.
dtparam=i2c_arm=on      # ADS1115 ADC (volume / switch / buttons)
dtparam=i2s=on          # I2S DAC
dtparam=spi=on          # ST7789 display

# Hardware watchdog (BCM2835): exposes /dev/watchdog so the BusyBox `watchdog`
# applet (started by /etc/init.d/S14watchdog) can arm the SoC's watchdog. If the
# whole system ever wedges, the board hard-resets on its own. Enabled in the
# kernel via board/radio/linux-watchdog.fragment (CONFIG_BCM2835_WDT).
dtparam=watchdog=on

# On-board audio off; an I2S DAC/amp is used instead
dtparam=audio=off

# Active DAC overlay — change to match your board.
dtoverlay=iqaudio-dacplus
#dtoverlay=hifiberry-dacplus
#dtoverlay=merus-amp

# No device_tree= line: this is a 32-bit build and the VideoCore firmware
# auto-loads the base DTB by board revision using the *downstream* name
# (bcm2710-rpi-3-b-plus.dtb for the 3A+), which we build via
# BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_INTREE_DTS_NAME. On this proven 32-bit base the auto-load
# works, so no custom device_tree= is needed (and none is shipped).

# Boot-speed/headless options: the ones applied in this file are disable_splash=1,
# boot_delay=0 and initial_turbo=30 (see below/above).
# gpu_mem is set via gpu_mem_512=100 (kept generous while the HDMI/framebuffer
# path stays debuggable). The more aggressive headless options
# (camera_auto_detect=0, display_auto_detect=0, a small gpu_mem=16) are NOT
# applied here and can be introduced one at a time after a confirmed bootable
# checkpoint.

# Boot optimization: no firmware splash / no artificial boot delay.
disable_splash=1
boot_delay=0
initial_turbo=30
